text.p: The Russian Central Bank expects inflation to ease to 5-8 percent next year and will to continue its currency policy of 1996 and 1997, chairman Sergei Dubinin told a banking conference on Wednesday.

Dubinin said next year the bank aimed for a smooth devaluation of the rouble against the dollar. "The stabilisation of the hard currency rate must take place within the framework of the course we maintained in 1996 and 1997," he said.
The rouble currently trades in a sloping corridor pegged to the dollar with rates calculated through the end of 1997.

"Plans which exist within the government and the Central Bank allow us to say with assurance that in 1998, provided we finish 1997 successfully, inflation should fall to 5-8 percent annually," he said.
Russian consumer prices rose 22 percent last year, but the government expects it to fall sharply this year.
Original forecasts were for a 1997 inflation rate of 11.8 percent but new figures presented to parliament this week put the rate at between 11.8 percent and 14 percent.
